findings.claim: The key Roman Olympians were: Jupiter, Juno, Neptune, Vulcan, Mercury, Mars, Pluto, Apollo, Juno, Venus, Minerva, Diana, Bacchus, Vesta and Ceres.
findings.truth: Juno appears once in the required Roman list; the second occurrence is a duplicate.

findings.claim: Livy records that after the fall of Troy, Aeneas led a band of survivors westward, eventually arriving in Italy and founding a settlement at Alba Longa, whose line of kings eventually included Rhea Silvia — and thus Romulus and Remus.
findings.truth: In the Roman foundation tradition, Aeneas founded Lavinium; his son Ascanius later founded Alba Longa.
findings.evidence: Livy 1.3; fetched Alba Longa reference, Legendary history and Founding myth

findings.claim: But before she leaves, Hades gives her pomegranate seeds to eat.
findings.truth: Hades secretly gives Persephone one pomegranate seed.
findings.evidence: Homeric Hymn to Demeter 370, 404; fetched Theoi text

findings.claim: She would spend part of each year with her mother on earth (spring and summer — when Demeter rejoices and the earth blooms) and part of each year with Hades below (autumn and winter — when Demeter grieves and the crops die).
findings.truth: The prescribed Hymn gives Persephone one third of the year below and two thirds with Demeter and the other gods; it does not give an equal seasonal split.
findings.evidence: Homeric Hymn to Demeter 400–404, 441–446; fetched Theoi text

findings.claim: Those without payment were left to wander on the near bank for a hundred years before Charon would take them across for free.
findings.truth: In Virgil's account, unburied souls wait for one hundred years before they can cross; the delay is not caused by failure to pay a fare.

findings.claim: The message was transparent to any educated Greek viewer: the Lapiths represented Athens and the Greeks; the Centaurs represented the Persians, who had invaded Greece in 480–479 BC and been driven back by Athenian courage.
findings.truth: A Persian-Wars reading is a common modern interpretation, not an established message transparent to every ancient viewer. Other readings foreground social order or the myth itself. Either qualify the claim throughout the lesson as an interpretation, or retain it only alongside alternatives.
findings.evidence: spec 2c, prescribed sources: learners must consider possible interpretations by different audiences
findings.ruling: Labelled as one modern reading with alternatives named.

findings.claim: The dead were ferried across the Acheron (not the Styx) by Charon.
findings.truth: Greek sources often place Charon on the Acheron, while Roman poets also name the Styx; Virgil associates him with both. Replace the categorical wording across the lesson with source-specific wording, or teach both traditions.
findings.evidence: fetched Charon reference, The Acheron and the Styx; Virgil, Aeneid 6
findings.ruling: Source-dependent wording in both glossary entries; coin-on-eyes dropped.

findings.claim: The music was so beautiful and so full of grief that it moved the king and queen of the dead to tears.
findings.truth: Ovid says the ghosts wept and the Eumenides' cheeks became wet with tears; the rulers grant Orpheus's request but are not said to weep. Correct every recurrence together, including the conclusion, practice material and flashcard, or remove the specific attribution.
findings.ruling: Ovid's attribution corrected in prose, takeaway and flashcard.

findings.claim: Livy, writing a careful history of Rome, included the Romulus and Remus story while acknowledging that such tales “adorn” the origins of cities.
findings.truth: The single-word quotation is not tied to a translation and could not be verified against a fetchable Livy text in this check. Treat it as a paraphrase unless the source edition is supplied.
findings.evidence: Direct fetch of the cited Livy text was unavailable in this session

summary: Five verified factual issues have surgical fixes. Three source-interpretation or cross-field issues need an editorial decision, and one quotation is recorded as unverified.
